title: Optimize / Evals review — 1:1 prep + follow-ups
content:
Meeting: Optimize / Evals review (weekly) — prep notes + follow-ups
Owners: Jamie Park (notes), Alex Kim (metric deep-dive), Priya Singh (prompt engineering)
Date: 2026-03-03 (weekly sync) — prep for 1:1 with Priya on 2026-03-04
Purpose: triage recent quality regressions surfaced by regressions-alert, prioritize prompt set updates and A/B rollbacks/rollouts, and assign owners for quick fixes and investigate root causes.

Agenda (30–45m):
- Quick status: alerts summary (3–5m)
- Deep-dive: top regression (A/B exp #342) — metric slide + example failures (15m)
- Prompt set hygiene: stale examples, overlap, adversarial cases (8m)
- Action items: canary/rollback plan, eval re-runs, tests to add (8–12m)

Summary of alerts (pulled from dashboard at 10:00 PST):
- Regression EVALS-1472: +6.8% drop in ROUGE-L on prompt-set "customer-qa-2025" for model v3b-quant. Triggered by batch on 2026-02-26.
- Regression EVALS-1481: small but persistent degradation in safety classifiers on open-domain prompts after tokenization change.
- A/B experiment #342 (rollout to 20%): higher factuality false negatives on finance prompts (precision down 4.2 pts).

Quick notes / hypotheses:
- v3b-quant kernel change (PR 312) likely altered tokenization/embedding alignment; could impact generation continuity for long-context prompts.
- Prompt-set "customer-qa-2025" contains ~12 examples with truncated context — might be sensitive to kv-cache alignment. Need to re-run failing examples with kv-cache debugging flags.
- Safety classifier drift may be due to preprocessing change (trim whitespace before tokenization) introduced in infra patch INF-890.

Representative failing examples (redacted):
- PROMPT ID: c-qa-2025-07 — user asks for refund policy with multi-turn context. Expected: clear policy summary + steps. Actual: missing last-step and hallucinated external policy.
- PROMPT ID: finance-ab-03 — question about interest rate calculation. Expected: numeric calculation + explanation. Actual: incorrect arithmetic and omitted units.
(Will attach full examples to Confluence page under linked_artifacts for audit)

Deep-dive plan (what I will ask Alex to run during sync):
- Metric diffs by slice: prompt-length bins (<128, 128–512, >512), domain slices (customer-support, finance, legal), tokenization changes between commit tags.
- Re-run baseline evals for v3b-quant with previous kernel (before PR 312) to confirm delta is introduced by that PR.
- For A/B #342: compute per-prompt precision/recall and confidence; capture top 20 false negatives for manual review.

Prompt-set hygiene (what Priya and I will do):
- Quick sweep to mark stale examples in "customer-qa-2025" (expected 30–40m): remove 3 duplicates found, re-add full dialog context for 12 truncated examples.
- Add 25 adversarial examples to the finance prompt set focusing on unit/number edge cases.
- Update eval metadata to include source/tag and expected tokens to better detect truncation-induced failures.

Canary / rollback recommendations:
- Immediate: rollback A/B experiment #342 to baseline at 30% -> 0% if precision drop persists after triage (owner: Product Ops).
- For v3b-quant: pin traffic to previous kernel for Dedicated customers with high finance traffic until we repro fix in staging (owner: Release Eng — Alex to raise RFC).

Short-term action items (owners + due dates):
- Alex: run slice diffs + re-run baseline with pre-PR312 kernel; create short runbook with findings. Due: 2026-03-05. Linked: github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/312
- Priya: prompt-set sweep + add 25 finance adversarial examples; update metadata tags. Due: 2026-03-06.
- Jamie: create canary rollback plan doc, update Confluence with failing examples and link to EVALS-1472. Due: 2026-03-04 (before 1:1).
- SRE/Infra (assign later): validate preprocessing change INF-890 impact on safety classifier; if confirmed, revert or patch. Initiate ticket INF-912. Due: 2026-03-07.

Tests to add (short list):
- Unit/regression tests that run the 20 top-failing finance prompts through the exact tokenization/preproc pipeline used in production. (owner: Eng QE)
- Add an automated check: when a new kernel PR touches tokenization or embedding hooks, trigger a reduced eval suite including financial and multi-turn customer support sets. (owner: Release Eng)

Notes to self / things to mention in 1:1 with Priya:
- Emphasize quick wins: small prompt edits can fix ~40% of examples, so prioritize those first for unblock.
- We should add a short checklist for prompt review before eval commit (length, full-dialog context, expected tokens).
- Consider a small canary of enhanced decoding params (temp/beam) on 5% traffic to test quick mitigate before code rollback.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we prefer rollback of kernel (which affects many customers) or targeted model pinning by route? Tradeoffs: blast radius vs operational complexity.
- How aggressive to be with A/B rollback threshold? Current threshold is 3% precision drop — should we tighten for finance domain?

Next steps / next meeting:
- Follow-up huddle 2026-03-04 11:00 PST (15m) — quick status on Alex runs + Priya prompt edits.
- Full weekly review 2026-03-10 — include SRE and Release Eng for infra rollback decision.

Attachments / places to check:
- Confluence: Optimize dashboard + full failing examples (linked_artifacts)
- Jira: EVALS-1472, EVALS-1481, INF-890, INF-912 (new)
- GitHub: PR 312 (kernel change), PR 319 (prompt set edits draft)

Random scratchpad thoughts (note-to-self):
- Could we add a lightweight "tokenization diff" tool that shows token alignment for two kernel versions? Would speed triage.
- Short-term: build a tiny script to re-run single prompt with kv-cache debug flags; reduce manual repro time from ~45m -> ~5m.

End of notes.
